title: Cache-read teaching example
summary: A caller asks for an item. This tiny cache-aside example returns its value, using a local cache to avoid reading the origin again.
audience: A developer meeting this code for the first time.
revision: Cache-read teaching fixture · app.py in this repository
scope: Two sequential reads of one unchanged item. Synthetic Python objects: no server, network, or database.

scenarios.title: Read an item for the first time
scenarios.summary: The empty cache sends this read to the origin; the result is saved for next time.
scenarios.trigger: demo() calls read_item with an empty cache.
scenarios.outcome: The caller gets blue mug; the cache now holds the same value.

steps.title: Ask for item-1
steps.detail: Create a cache and an origin, then pass both to the read function.

steps.title: Look in the cache
steps.detail: The key is absent, so this request continues past the early-return branch.

steps.title: Read the original value
steps.detail: The origin returns blue mug and increments its read counter.

steps.title: Keep a copy for the next read
steps.detail: read_item stores the returned value under item-1 before responding.

steps.title: Return blue mug
steps.detail: The function returns the value directly; no later delivery step is involved.

branches.condition: If the key is already cached
branches.path: read_item returns at line 19. It skips both the origin read and the cache write; see the second scenario.
All calls are synchronous. Origin owns the original value; the cache stores a derived copy.

scenarios.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Caller
    participant R as read_item
    participant K as Cache dict
    participant O as Origin
    C->>R: Request item-1
    R->>K: Look up item-1
    K-->>R: Not cached
    R->>O: Read item-1
    O-->>R: blue mug
    R->>K: Save blue mug
    R-->>C: Return blue mug

reading.title: Start with the caller
reading.detail: Read demo, then read_item. The two successive calls show where the second request takes a different path.

scenarios.title: Read the same item again
scenarios.summary: The stored copy answers this request; the origin is not called a second time.
scenarios.trigger: demo() makes a second call with the same cache and origin.
scenarios.outcome: The caller gets blue mug again; the origin read count stays at one.

steps.title: Request item-1 again
steps.detail: The second call reuses the objects from the first call, including its cached value.

steps.title: Find the stored value
steps.detail: The key is present, so the function takes the cache-hit branch.

steps.title: Return directly from the cache
steps.detail: The early return avoids the origin call below it. check() asserts equal responses and one origin read.

branches.path: An existing cache entry is not refreshed. This fixture contains no invalidation or expiry policy.

scenarios.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Caller
    participant R as read_item
    participant K as Cache dict
    participant O as Origin
    C->>R: Request item-1 again
    R->>K: Look up item-1
    K-->>R: blue mug
    Note over R,O: Cache hit returns without calling Origin
    R-->>C: Return blue mug

omitted: Missing keys, origin failures, concurrent requests, process restarts, and distributed consistency.
The example makes no production freshness or latency claim. Its runnable check covers equal responses and the origin read count.

features.title: Read an item
features.description: Fetch an item from the origin and keep a copy in memory.

features.title: Read it again
features.description: Reuse the cached value without another origin read.

stack.name: Python 3 · standard library
stack.purpose: One synchronous script. argparse selects the demo or its assertion-based check.

stack.name: In-process Python objects
stack.purpose: A dict caches values; Origin is also an in-memory object. There is no external database, middleware, or network service in this fixture.

structureSummary: A single-module teaching fixture: start with the executable example, then follow either read scenario. It has no application or library package hierarchy.

packages.name: Cache-read module
packages.responsibility: Origin owns the original values. read_item performs the cache lookup and fill; demo runs two reads, and check verifies the returned values and origin read count.
